text: Ireland’s headline fiscal balance is projected to remain in surplus during 2026–31, masking underlying long-term fiscal vulnerabilities. Annual revenue growth averages about 6 percent during 2026–30, while the structural primary balance deteriorates by about 0.6 percent of GDP (1.0 percent of GNI*) in 2026. Public debt is projected to decline to about 26 percent of GDP (about 50 percent of GNI*) in 2031. Ireland is assessed to remain at low risk of sovereign stress. Staff recommends maintaining a broadly neutral fiscal stance, strengthening expenditure controls, broadening the tax base, and adopting a binding national fiscal rule.
